summary: A worker-placement game where each worker type (raiders, horses, etc.) resolves differently based on a die roll, sending you around the board collecting resources to fulfill contracts and build up your tribe. It plays like a lighter cousin of Phillips' North Sea/West Kingdom games, with the same contract-fulfillment engine and a Mongol-steppe reskin.
criticised: Very similar to Phillips' other Garphill games, feels derivative
Dice mitigation can feel swingy for some workers

interaction.kind: worker placement on shared action spots plus contract/resource competition
interaction.detail: Players place workers of different types on a shared row of action spaces and compete for limited contract cards and resources, so a popular spot or contract can be denied to you by an opponent taking it first. Most of the turn, though, is spent developing your own tribe/warband and fulfilling your own contracts, so the board is more contested than a pure engine-builder but not adversarial.

scoring.how_you_win: Place worker dice each turn to gather resources, fulfill contracts along the trade route, raid villages and build your homestead; the player with the most accumulated VP when the deck/track runs out wins.
